title: Expose typed room topology and assignment APIs
description: Strengthen the existing room endpoints for the interactive matrix. Return alphabetized room topology, persist sensor movement immediately, reject invalid assignments, provide duplicate-safe room rename behavior, and expose calculated room humidity with FCU status.
design: Use Pydantic request and response models with unknown fields forbidden on the new or changed control contracts, consistent with the concern in hvac-obp. Treat Unassigned as a typed presentation group for room_id NULL. Reject assignment of ERV and INTERNAL devices and prevent moving an FCU away from its owned room. Return 409 for duplicate rename targets.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown rooms and devices return clear errors; invalid device types cannot be assigned; duplicate room names return 409; successful moves are immediately visible in status and calculations; FCU status includes calculated room humidity; Flask client tests verify real SQLite persistence.

title: Bootstrap room topology and FCU discovery lifecycle
description: Add persistence, migration, and discovery behavior that maintains one room per FCU. Existing FCUs each get a room and join it. Existing physical non-ERV non-FCU devices remain room_id NULL and appear as Unassigned. New FCUs create and join a room automatically. This also completes the discovery expectations in GitHub #153 and must enforce device_type rather than relying on the one-shot backfill noted in hvac-a9u.
design: Use a Flyway schema migration plus an idempotent typed reconciliation service for data bootstrap. Generate names from display_name then device_name, suffixing collisions as Name (2), Name (3), and so on. Keep ERV and INTERNAL devices outside room assignment. Do not update the manually refreshed production DB during tests.
acceptance_criteria: Every FCU has exactly one room; no room has more than one FCU; new FCU discovery creates and assigns a room transactionally; duplicate defaults get numbered suffixes; physical non-FCU devices remain Unassigned; ERV and INTERNAL devices remain excluded; discovery always persists a valid device_type; SQLite tests run through the Makefile.

title: Refactor shared room metric source selection
description: Extract one typed mechanism that selects current, non-stale metric readings belonging to a room. Reuse it for FCU temperature, room humidity, and room-oriented presentation data. This is a scoped implementation of the service-layer direction in GitHub #127.
design: Add a focused app/room_metrics.py service with Pydantic source and aggregate models. Centralize room membership, physical-device eligibility, latest-reading selection, metric extraction, and the 10-minute stale cutoff. Keep raw SQLite queries in db.py and pass explicit inputs rather than Flask request state.
acceptance_criteria: One source-selection path serves temperature and humidity; stale, out-of-room, ERV, and INTERNAL readings are excluded; missing metrics are handled explicitly; service inputs and outputs are typed; substantive SQLite tests cover stale boundaries and mixed sensor payloads without mocks.

title: Apply room membership to FCU temperature and room humidity
description: Make room membership determine FCU metric eligibility. Temperature keeps existing fcu_temp_sources weights, but only weighted sources currently assigned to the FCU room participate. Humidity is the equal-weight arithmetic mean of every current in-room humidity source. This defines the room-temperature data used by GitHub #62 and must honor the missing-data behavior in GitHub #117.
design: Leave out-of-room weights persisted but inactive so moving a sensor back restores its weight. Apply current room membership and current weights to historical calculated series, matching existing weight semantics. Remove the raw FCU fallback when its reading is stale. Emit or preserve chart gap markers so stale intervals are not visually connected as valid data.
acceptance_criteria: Moving a sensor changes the next FCU calculation; temperature uses existing weights only for in-room sources; humidity uses equal weights; no usable humidity yields None; all aggregates exclude readings older than 10 minutes; historical charts do not bridge stale intervals; tests cover moves, restored weights, stale boundaries, and missing data.

title: Implement rooms as canonical FCU and sensor topology
description: Make rooms the shared topology for FCUs, physical non-ERV devices, the main Air Quality matrix, calculated FCU temperature, and calculated room humidity. Every FCU owns a room whose default name is the FCU display name. Physical non-ERV devices may be in a room or the virtual Unassigned group; ERVs and INTERNAL pseudo-devices remain outside the room model. GitHub issue #144 is the canonical umbrella; #143 is already closed after friendly-name work.
design: Use devices.room_id as the single membership mechanism. Preserve fcu_temp_sources weights for temperature but restrict eligible sources to the FCU room. Humidity is an equal-weight mean. Represent Unassigned as room_id NULL rather than a duplicate special room row.
acceptance_criteria: One room exists per FCU; discovery creates rooms safely; the Air Quality matrix is grouped and editable by room; FCU temperature and humidity use only non-stale in-room sources; ERV and INTERNAL devices remain excluded; documentation and substantive Makefile-driven tests are current.

title: Flyway migrations run against live, cron-written 138MB SQLite DB without quiescing
description:
Context: Flyway adoption (PR #124) wired 'make deploy' on host slg1 to run 'flyway migrate' against the production SQLite DB. The deploy target does NOT stop the every-minute cron runner (bin/runner.py) before migrating; it runs: git pull -> poetry install -> flyway validate -> cp backup -> flyway migrate -> flyway validate.

Problem: SQLite is single-writer. bin/runner.py writes to the same DB file every minute via cron. During a migration the two collide:
- V5__normalize_devlog_time_values.sql is a FULL-TABLE UPDATE over devlog, which in production is 778,213 rows / ~138MB. While it runs it holds a write lock.
- A concurrent cron write hits SQLITE_BUSY / 'database is locked'. Either the runner loses a minute of data or the migration fails, depending on timing. Note paths.py sets TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 2, a very short busy timeout.
- Worst case: a migration failing mid-flight leaves flyway_schema_history marking it failed, requiring a manual 'flyway repair' before the next deploy succeeds.

Evidence: verified against a fresh prod snapshot (devlog count 778213, DB file 138MB). The Makefile 'deploy' target contains no service/cron stop.

Fix direction: quiesce the cron runner (or take the app offline) for the duration of 'make deploy', or at minimum bracket 'flyway migrate' with the runner disabled and re-enable after. Treat quiescing as the default for any future data migration, not an exception.
acceptance_criteria: make deploy stops/pauses the every-minute runner before flyway migrate and restores it after; document the quiescing in doc/sql-migrations.md

title: Add sensor drag-drop and room rename interactions
description: Add desktop and touchscreen management to the grouped matrix. Sensor drops persist immediately. Right-click and touch long-press on a room separator open the same rename dialog.
design: Create a self-contained app/static/room_matrix.js using pointer events. Optimistically move rows, but restore the original section and show an error on failed persistence. Re-sort groups after rename. Keep Unassigned non-renamable. Test pure gesture and state-transition logic in Node; do not add Playwright, consistent with hvac-7mx.
acceptance_criteria: Mouse and touch moves share one save path; one drop makes one request; failed saves restore the row; ordinary taps do not trigger long-press; duplicate names remain editable with a clear error; successful rename reorders sections without reload; Makefile JS tests cover meaningful interaction logic.

title: Refactor FCU Room Editor and dashboard value formatting
description: Update the existing FCU Room Editor and status renderer to consume the shared room-derived contract. Show active in-room temperature candidates, calculated room humidity, and the agreed display precision.
design: Filter active candidates by room while retaining stored weights for sources that move out. Refresh candidates after assignment changes. Populate FCU humidity from the API rather than browser-side aggregation. Render humidity as an integer, Celsius with decimal precision, Fahrenheit as whole degrees, and missing values as --.
acceptance_criteria: Out-of-room sources cannot affect FCU temperature; stored weights survive moving out and back; FCU humidity updates from status; humidity has no decimal places; Celsius has decimals and Fahrenheit does not; stale-only rooms display --; existing raw versus calculated chart labels remain explicit.

title: Document and verify the rooms implementation
description: Update durable room documentation and run integration verification. Record relationships to GitHub #144, #153, #127, #62, #117, #32, #107, #152, and #158, distinguishing implemented scope from downstream work.
design: Update calculated-temperatures-and-rooms.md, rooms-implementation-review.md, and agent-index.md. Document FCU-owned rooms, virtual Unassigned, exclusions, name collision rules, weighted temperature, equal-weight humidity, stale gaps, migration bootstrap, and rollback considerations. Follow the repository Flyway safety guidance and related hvac-kag and hvac-9ai concerns.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation matches the final schema and APIs; downstream issue boundaries are explicit; migration and rollback steps are documented; relevant Makefile checks pass; tests do not modify var/db/temperature-bot.db; the implementation has no pro-forma or mock-heavy tests.

title: Render the Air Quality matrix by room
description: Render one Air Quality table containing alphabetically ordered room sections, including empty rooms and the virtual Unassigned group. Each displayed sensor occurs under exactly one room separator.
design: Prepare typed room-group view models in routes_web.py. Keep one shared header and tbody. Render a thick separator with the room name overlaid on the left before each group. Preserve existing metric links, notes, thresholds, update summaries, and the browser C/F preference from GitHub #25.
acceptance_criteria: Rooms appear alphabetically; empty rooms remain visible; every displayed physical sensor appears exactly once; Unassigned contains room_id NULL sensors; FCUs, ERVs, and INTERNAL devices are not draggable sensor rows; route and template tests verify the grouping contract.

title: Flyway is forward-only; prod rollback relies solely on a cp-based DB backup
description:
Context: Flyway Community has no undo/down migrations. The only rollback path is the timestamped backup that 'make deploy' takes before migrating: cp -f $PROD_DB $PROD_BACKUP_DIR/temperature-bot.<UTC>.db

Problems with the current backup-as-rollback story:
1. Torn-page risk: 'cp' of a live SQLite file while the every-minute cron runner may be writing can capture an inconsistent (torn) snapshot. Use 'sqlite3 $PROD_DB ".backup ..."' or 'VACUUM INTO' instead, which take a consistent snapshot. (Relates to the quiescing bug.)
2. No retention/pruning: each deploy copies a full ~138MB file into PROD_BACKUP_DIR with no cleanup visible -> unbounded disk growth.
3. Recovery is all-or-nothing: a bad migration is undone only by restoring the whole DB and redeploying; any rows written between migrate and rollback are lost.

Fix direction: switch the backup to a consistent SQLite snapshot mechanism, add backup retention (keep N most recent), and document the restore procedure in doc/sql-migrations.md.
acceptance_criteria: deploy uses a consistent-snapshot backup (sqlite3 .backup / VACUUM INTO); backup retention policy exists; restore procedure documented

title: CLAUDE.md still says 'no migration framework / manual ALTER' after Flyway adoption
description:
Context: Flyway is now the migration framework (PR #124, V1-V6 applied in prod). But temperature-bot/CLAUDE.md still states: 'Schema lives in etc/schema.sql; no migration framework -- production changes are manual ALTER statements.'

Problem: This stale guidance actively tells contributors (and AI agents starting fresh sessions) to do the wrong thing:
- Hand-applying ALTER statements to prod bypasses Flyway entirely and is not recorded in flyway_schema_history.
- Hand-editing etc/schema.sql is now forbidden (it is a generated artifact from 'make schema'), but the doc still presents it as the source of truth. Because schema.sql is checked in and tests run against it, a hand-edit makes TESTS PASS while the Flyway migration history is missing the change -> silent dev/prod schema drift.

Fix: update both CLAUDE.md (project) and any other doc that references the manual-ALTER workflow to point at doc/sql-migrations.md, state that etc/schema.sql is generated (never hand-edit), and that all schema changes go through a new Vn__*.sql migration.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md no longer claims 'no migration framework'; it directs schema changes through Flyway migrations and marks etc/schema.sql as generated

title: [bug] FCU Off jumps back to Auto on main page
description: On the main FCU grid (index.html / unit_speed.js), switching a unit from Auto to Off briefly shows Off, then reverts to Auto on the next status refresh. Root cause: the radio-selection logic in unit_speed.js checks speedValue===-1 (Auto) BEFORE isOff, so an off unit holding Auto speed (fan_speed=-1, which the AE200 retains because set_body_drive never resets FanSpeed) re-checks the Auto radio. Violates one-dimensional control principle. room_dashboard.js already does it correctly (isOff first).
notes:
DESIGN (approved, fix both):
Fix1 (display, unit_speed.js): reorder radio-selection so isOff is checked BEFORE the Auto(-1) branch, matching the already-correct room_dashboard.js:233. Extract decision into pure fanRadioIdForDevice(dev) returning a radio element id (or null) so it's unit-testable under node; guard window.* refs and add module.exports (mirrors temperature_utils.js pattern).
Fix2 (readback race, rules_engine.py): set_body_drive/set_body_fan_speed re-read hardware via get_device_info immediately after sending the command, which on real hardware can capture stale pre-change state. Override the just-commanded field (Drive / FanSpeed) on the readback dict before insert_devlog_entry so the recorded status reflects intent. (Simulator mutates synchronously so it can't reproduce the race; covered by a unit test mocking a stale readback.)
Tests: tests/test_unit_speed.js (node) for fanRadioIdForDevice incl. off-was-Auto; python test mocking stale get_device_info to assert override. Add JS test to Makefile.
close_reason: Fixed Off→Auto jump. Display: reordered fan-radio selection in unit_speed.js so isOff precedes the Auto(-1) branch (extracted to testable fanRadioIdForDevice). Race: set_body_drive/set_body_fan_speed now record the commanded value instead of a possibly-stale hardware read-back. Tests: tests/test_unit_speed.js + 2 readback-race tests in test_endpoints.py; verified end-to-end against real /status payload (Bamboo/Broadway South off-was-Auto now resolve to Off).

title: Room dashboard drops a button press made during in-flight request
description: setDeviceLoading disables all of a device's speed buttons while a set request is in flight. A press landing in that window is silently dropped by the browser (disabled buttons fire no click), so the unit stays in its prior state (e.g. LO->Off->MED leaves it Off/'was LO' because MED was swallowed). Intermittent because the row is re-enabled by either the set response or the 10s poll, so timing decides whether a press lands. The disabling predates the optimistic UI, which now handles rapid presses (last-press-wins + reconcile). Fix: stop disabling buttons; keep the spinner feedback.

title: Room dashboard: optimistic UI update on fan speed/drive change
description: Changing a unit (e.g. HI->Off) does not always update the room dashboard immediately. handleSpeedButton issues the set API then calls refreshStatus(), but the backend re-reads the AE200 right after commanding it and on real hardware that read-back can still show the old state, so /status returns stale data until a later poll settles. Fix: optimistically render the intended state on click, and hold it until a poll confirms (common case) or a backstop window elapses (silent failure). Reconcile per-device so polls don't revert a not-yet-settled change.
notes: Implemented optimistic UI: applyOptimisticChange() renders the intended drive/speed on click and records a pending change keyed by device_id. updateDeviceStatus reconciles each poll — keeps the optimistic state until incoming data matches (matchesPending) or PENDING_RECONCILE_MS (60s) backstop elapses; clears + renders truth otherwise. Error path drops pending and re-polls. Extracted renderDriveState() shared by polled + optimistic paths. Verified via mocked-stale /status (Playwright, one-off, not committed): Off click holds across 3 stale polls then reconciles. No browser test added (project moving away from Playwright).

title: Off+Auto leaves Auto button highlighted on room dashboard
description: On the room dashboard, turning an FCU off while its held speed is Auto leaves BOTH the Off button and the Auto button highlighted. updateButtonActiveState() in room_dashboard.js marks the Auto button active when currentSpeed==-1 regardless of drive state (a leftover from the orthogonal on/off-vs-speed model). Under the one-dimensional model, when off only Off should be active; the held Auto is historical (shown as 'was Auto'). Numeric speeds already require !isOff, so only Auto was affected.

title: Show friendly fan-speed names instead of raw 'Speed N' / protocol codes
description:
User complained that 'OFF (Speed 4)' on the Hickory (room dashboard) status line makes no sense. Root cause: the status line shows raw 'Speed N' rather than the friendly labels (HI/MED/LO/Auto) already used on the control buttons. Drive (on/off) and fan speed are orthogonal in the AE200 model, so an off unit still reports its held speed.

Scope (confirmed with user):
1. room_dashboard.js status line: ON shows friendly label (e.g. 'HI'); OFF shows 'OFF (was HI)'. Read the label off the matching speed button in the DOM so it's device-type-correct (ERV vs fan) with no duplicated map.
2. alerts.html 'Fan: <raw>' currently shows the protocol code (HIGH/MID1/MID2/LOW/AUTO). Map to friendly labels server-side in db_alerts (device_name + raw fan_speed both available), exposing a display field.

Out of scope: unifying index.html en-dash 'Med–Low' vs room 'MED-LO' styling (leave as-is).
notes:
Decisions: (1) Room status line reads friendly label from matching DOM speed button (no duplicated JS map; device-type-correct for free). ON='HI' etc; OFF='OFF (was HI)'; Auto-while-off kept as 'OFF (Auto)' (Auto is a mode, not a level it ran at). (2) Alerts: add ae200.friendly_fan_speed_label(device_name, raw) mapping protocol code->number (FAN_SPEED_NAMES)->friendly per device type (ERV vs fan), matching button vocab; applied in db_alerts get_active_alerts/get_alert_history as details['fan_speed_display']; alerts.html uses it. Accepted unavoidable duplication: button labels (DOM) vs Python helper, since alerts has no buttons; keep them matching + cross-ref comment. Out of scope: index/button styling, en-dash unification.
Final UX (after user review of first cut): rejected the header speed label entirely. ON state shows no speed text (the glowing button is the one-dimensional source of truth). OFF state shows the prior speed as a small 'was HI' historical note ON the Off button (the selected control) — NOT a 'resume target' on a speed button, since exposing a resume action would re-introduce the orthogonal model we deliberately hide. Alerts portion (friendly_fan_speed_label) unchanged from plan.

title: Remove Area 51 fan from Hickory room page
description: Remove the 'Area 51' FCU/fan from the hickory room dashboard. It should no longer render as a speed-control row on the /hickory page. The underlying device is not being decommissioned — just hidden from this page. Scope: app/room_config.py only (plus the test that pins the config). Do NOT touch the building map page (map.html/map0.html) or any data fixtures.
notes: Decision: Remove 'Area 51' from hickory fans list in room_config.py. Also REMOVE test_room_config_hickory_has_fcu_devices (test_routes.py) entirely rather than trim it — with only Restrooms/BOH left as a speed-controlled FCU it no longer guards anything; the [0]-slice regression is already covered by test_filter_speed_control_returns_all_matches (config-independent). Out of scope: map page (map.html/map0.html), hubitat-area51.js, air-quality fixture, _FAKE_SPEED_DEVICES unit data.

title: Add per-metric click-to-chart for Air Quality columns
description:
Main-page Air Quality columns (Humidity, CO2, VOC, Radon, PM2.5, PM1) should behave like Temperature and Illuminance: clicking a cell opens a time-series chart for that metric, with the clicked device pre-selected and all other devices available as checkboxes.

Data: all six metrics are already logged to devlog.status_json every minute via update_from_airthings; full per-device history exists.

Approach: single parameterized /metric_chart?metric=<name>&device_ids=<id> page + /api/v1/metric?metric=<name> endpoint, mirroring the illuminance chart pattern. Cell links only rendered when that device actually has data for that metric (same pattern as has_illuminance).

Out of scope (follow-on): CSV download on metric and lighting chart pages.
notes:
Design decisions:
- One parameterized page + one parameterized API endpoint, not six copies. Config table maps URL metric name -> {status_json key, display label, unit, y-axis formatter, decimals}. Note radon's URL name 'radon' maps to status_json key 'radonShortTermAvg'.
- New db helper get_device_metric_series(conn, status_key, value_path, device_ids) generalizes get_lighting_series. Values are nested as status_json[key].value (Airthings structure); helper must unwrap.
- Per-device/per-metric gating: get_device_status extended to set has_humidity/has_co2/has_voc/has_radon/has_pm25/has_pm1 booleans, mirroring has_illuminance logic. Template only renders chart link when the flag is set.
- Radon chart must respect user's existing Bq/m3 <-> pCi/L unit preference (currently honored in unit_speed.js).
- CSV download deferred to hvac-yhq; will be added to both this new page and the lighting chart at the same time.
Implementation complete and verified via curl + unit tests. All 6 metric pages render (200), invalid metric rejected (400), API returns per-device series correctly filtered by device_ids. Cell gating verified: Airthings devices expose all 6 metric links, Hubitat sensors expose only humidity (matches their data). Radon tooltip precision fixed per advisor: 1 decimal in pCi/L mode, 0 in Bq/m³.

Awaiting browser verification from user (CLI environment can't launch browser):
- Click CO2 cell -> chart renders with clicked device pre-selected
- Click Hubitat humidity cell (e.g. device 15) -> cross-source data renders
- Radon chart + C/F toggle -> y-axis, tooltip unit, and values all rescale
- Temporal picker (day/week/month/all) -> reloads data

Tests added (all passing):
- test_get_device_metric_series_airthings_dict
- test_get_device_metric_series_hubitat_scalar
- test_get_device_metric_series_skips_missing
- test_get_device_status_sets_aq_metric_flags
- test_metric_endpoint_accepts_known_metrics
- test_metric_endpoint_rejects_unknown_metric
- test_metric_chart_page_renders
Browser-verified by user on 2026-04-21. Caught missing #metric-chart height CSS rule (chart div needs explicit height for echarts; ported 620px rule from #lighting-chart into style.css).
close_reason: Shipped. Per-metric click-to-chart for Humidity/CO2/VOC/Radon/PM2.5/PM1 on home page, browser-verified.

title: Add temperature controls to room table displays
description: Each room page should offer control of relevant FCU units (temperature and fan speed). Hickory: add FCU Restrooms/BOH, and add up/down temperature controls to both FCUs (Area 51 and Restrooms/BOH). ERVs should NOT get temperature controls. Kitchen: add the Kitchen FCU with controls.
notes: Design: Add set-temp up/down controls to room dashboard FCU cards (not ERVs). Device names: Restrooms/BOH (id=1) for Hickory, Kitchen (id=8) for Kitchen. Remove [filtered[0]] single-fan limit. Port setupSetTempControls/setDeviceSetTemp from unit_speed.js to room_dashboard.js.

title: Restyle remaining pages to match site conventions
description: Apply consistent styling (main-grid wrapper, h2 headings, data-table class, last-refresh timestamps) to: logs_today, rules, debug_all_devices, chart, chart_aqi, lighting_chart, about.

title: Restyle Deep Dive | Alerts page to match site conventions
description: The Deep Dive | Alerts page has inconsistent styling compared to other pages in the app. Update its CSS/HTML to match the best patterns used across the site (layout, tables, spacing, fonts, etc.).
notes: Design: wrap in #main-grid (max-width:none like weather), h1→h2, add aq-legend-style color legend, add last-refresh-inline timestamp with auto-refresh note, replace opacity:0.7 with border approach for alert rows, polish tab styling with border-bottom active indicator, tighten form spacing.

title: Rooms should not have Back buttons
description:
The rooms pages (Hickory and Kitchen) have a back button in the top left ("-> Main").
This is useful when the page is invoked from the app main menu.

But these pages are also intended to be used on standalone tables, where this escape
should not be offered.

So, make this conditional. The invocation from the app should add and `embedded` flag
parameter to the URL.

title: Enhance hickory page
description:
This issue includes several tasks.

Implement each one separately, and pause for the user to test each, before committing
and continuing to the next task. All of the tasks in this issue refer to the Hickory
room page.

Note that some backend support for this was added in recent commits 2370b69 and
a5e8e19. You will need to understand this code. You may also need to add additional
similar code to support some of these new features.

Note also that our work today replaces features that are already supported by a Hubitat
dashboard page:
http://10.2.3.51/apps/api/538/dashboard/538?access_token=a161dd5b-8f38-4323-8f2c-2f2ed330bb0e
You may find it useful to examine that page, since it my have some useful insights for

Here are the tasks:

# Task 2: Add the current date and time (just down to minutes; no seconds) to this
  page. It should update without the user needing to manually refresh.

title: Pydantic *Control request models use extra='ignore'; HVAC commands silently accept unknown/typo'd fields
description:
Context: app/models.py is the new typed contract layer. Request bodies for the control endpoints are validated by flask_pydantic @validate(): SpeedControl, DriveControl, ModeControl, NoteControl, DeviceMetadataControl, SetTempControl, SetRangeControl, DeviceRoomControl, FcuTempSourceControl. None of them set model_config extra='forbid', so they use Pydantic's default extra='ignore'.

Problem: a client that sends a misspelled or wrong field name gets a 200 with an UNINTENDED action rather than a 400. Example: POST /set_temp {"device_id": 12, "set_temp": 21} -- the real field is set_temp_c, so 'set_temp' is silently dropped and set_temp_c is treated as missing/defaulted. These endpoints command real HVAC hardware, so silently ignoring unknown fields is exactly where strict validation should catch the client bug.

Inconsistency: the extra policy across models.py is applied roughly inversely to where it helps. The *Control request bodies (where strictness catches client errors) are lenient (ignore), while WeatherData -- a response/parse model where leniency is usually safer -- is set to extra='forbid'. StatusPayload/CommandResponse/DeviceStatus use extra='allow' intentionally for vendor passthrough (fine).

Fix:
1. Set model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') on all *Control request models so typo'd/unknown fields return 400 (the existing _validation_error_response already returns 400 on ValidationError).
2. Audit/confirm WeatherData's extra='forbid' is intentional: if it ever parses an external weather API payload, an added upstream field would raise -- in that case it should be 'ignore'. If it only validates internally-assembled data, forbid is fine as a self-check.
3. Consider documenting a convention: request bodies = forbid, vendor-passthrough responses = allow, internal-only response models = forbid/ignore by intent.
acceptance_criteria: All *Control request models reject unknown fields with 400; WeatherData's extra policy is confirmed correct for its data source; the extra-policy convention is documented

title: PM1 air-quality coloring reuses PM2.5 thresholds (not standards-based)
description:
Context: app/static/air_quality_thresholds.json colors AQ table cells good/fair/poor. The 'pm1' entry has thresholds identical to 'pm25' (fairAbove 9, poorAbove 35.4 ug/m3).

Problem: those 9 / 35.4 figures are EPA PM2.5 numbers. PM1 is a finer size fraction fully contained within PM2.5, so PM1 <= PM2.5 by definition, and there is no recognized health standard for PM1. Consequences: (1) PM1 cells will almost never reach 'poor'; (2) when colored at all, the thresholds are borrowed/arbitrary rather than meaningful. This is a correctness/credibility issue for a health-facing display.

Fix direction: either drop PM1 coloring entirely, or set PM1-appropriate thresholds and document the basis, or explicitly annotate in the JSON/legend that PM1 uses PM2.5 breakpoints as a heuristic (not a standard).
acceptance_criteria: PM1 coloring is either removed, given a documented PM1-specific basis, or clearly annotated as a non-standard heuristic reuse of PM2.5 thresholds

title: DISCUSSION (David + Simson): align on a frontend testing strategy
description:
A decision/discussion issue for David and Simson. The recent main..origin/main batch pulls the project in two opposite directions on frontend testing at once, and the codebase now carries three overlapping approaches. We should agree on an intended strategy before more is built on either path.

=== Stated direction (prior intent) ===
The working assumption recorded for temperature-bot has been: 'moving away from Playwright browser tests; do not propose new ones.' The motivation (as understood) is that headless-browser tests are heavy, flaky, slow, and a maintenance burden, and that frontend logic is better covered by fast Node/JS unit tests. The repo does have a growing JS unit-test suite that fits this direction: tests/test_unit_speed.js (now ~600+ lines), test_metric_chart_support.js, test_air_quality_thresholds.js, test_temperature_utils.js, test_time_utils.js. These run without a browser and exercise frontend JS logic directly.

=== What this batch actually merged (new behavior) ===
Despite that direction, this batch ADDS Playwright in two places and reintroduces it as a hard dependency (pyproject.toml: playwright = '==1.60.0'):

1. New Playwright browser UX tests -- tests/test_browser_ux.py (new, ~98 lines): test_chart_page_no_dom_errors, test_air_quality_temperature_click_fetches_selected_device, test_chart_exclusion_set_persists_after_clear_all_and_range_change. These drive headless Chromium via playwright.sync_api. IMPORTANT: they are decorated @skip_on_github (conftest.py skips when GITHUB_ACTIONS=='true') and also gated on SKIP_BROWSER_TEST. So they run ONLY on a developer's local machine and NEVER in CI.

2. The web UI screenshot pipeline -- .github/workflows/web-ui-screenshots.yml + bin/render_web_ui_pages.py (~830 lines) + 'make web-screenshots'. On every PR it builds a temp SQLite DB, seeds fake data, starts Flask, and uses Playwright (headless Chromium) to screenshot each route, then posts the images inline in a sticky PR comment. This is screenshot RENDERING for human review, not assertion-based testing -- a defensible but distinct use of the same dependency.

=== The tension to resolve ===
- Stated 'avoid Playwright' vs. two new Playwright entry points landed in the same batch. Is Playwright now an accepted dependency (for rendering and/or local UX tests), or is it still slated for removal? The answer changes whether test_browser_ux.py should be invested in or deleted, and whether the screenshot pipeline should be kept.
- If Playwright stays for screenshots only, draw a clear line: 'Playwright is allowed for screenshot rendering, NOT for assertion tests; logic goes in JS unit tests.' If it stays for both, retire the 'avoid Playwright' guidance.

=== Concerns flagged (feed the discussion) ===
a) CI-skipped browser tests = false confidence. test_browser_ux.py is @skip_on_github, so it contributes zero coverage in CI. Local-only tests bit-rot silently (they pass for whoever wrote them, then drift). Either run them in CI (accepting the cost/flake) or be explicit that they are dev-only smoke checks and don't count as coverage.
b) Three parallel fake-data sources now exist and can drift: the hardware simulators (app/test_data/*, e.g. hubitat_get_devices.json), the pytest fixtures (etc/sample_hubitat.json + others), and the screenshot renderer's OWN inline fakes in bin/render_web_ui_pages.py (seed_devices/fake_hubitat_devices/fake_weather_data/ae200_status). Screenshots can therefore depict data shapes that diverge from what the real simulators and tests use. A strategy decision should include consolidating to one fake-data source. (See also hvac-sep, hvac-bqb on simulator-fixture fragmentation.)
c) Screenshot pipeline housekeeping: each PR creates a per-PR prerelease+tag (web-ui-screenshots-pr-<N>); assets are replaced per run but the release/tag is never deleted on PR close -> unbounded tag/release clutter. Worth a cleanup step if the pipeline is kept. (Could be split into its own issue once the keep/drop decision is made.)
d) Dependency weight: Playwright pins a browser download (Chromium) in CI and a 1.60.0 pin in pyproject; that is real install/cache cost on every screenshot run, justified only if the pipeline earns its keep in review.

=== Decisions sought ===
1. Is Playwright an accepted dependency going forward? For rendering only, for tests too, or neither (remove)?
2. What is the canonical layer for frontend correctness -- JS unit tests, browser tests, screenshot review, or a defined mix?
3. Should browser tests run in CI or remain local-only (and if local-only, are they 'tests' or 'smoke checks')?
4. Consolidate the three fake-data sources to one?
5. Keep the screenshot pipeline? If so, add release/tag cleanup-on-close.

Update the temperature-bot guidance docs (and the 'avoid Playwright' note) to match whatever is decided, so future contributors and AI agents get a single consistent signal.
acceptance_criteria: David and Simson agree on: (1) Playwright's status, (2) the canonical frontend-correctness layer, (3) CI vs local-only browser tests, (4) fake-data consolidation, (5) screenshot-pipeline keep/drop + cleanup; project guidance docs updated to match

title: Simulator env flags parse inconsistently: AE200_SIMULATOR/AIRTHINGS_SIMULATOR=0 (or false) enables, not disables
description:
Context: the three hardware simulators are toggled by env vars, but they parse those vars inconsistently.
- HUBITAT_SIMULATOR (app/hubitat.py): robust truthy check -- os.getenv(...).strip().lower() in {1,true,yes,on}. So '0'/'false'/'' correctly mean OFF.
- AE200_SIMULATOR (app/ae200.py:86): AE200_SIMULATOR = os.getenv('AE200_SIMULATOR') -- ANY non-empty string is truthy.
- AIRTHINGS_SIMULATOR (app/airthings.py:18): same raw os.getenv pattern -- ANY non-empty string is truthy.

Problem / footgun: AE200_SIMULATOR=0 or AE200_SIMULATOR=false -- the natural way to try to DISABLE the simulator -- actually ENABLES it, because '0' is a non-empty string. Same for AIRTHINGS_SIMULATOR. This is currently masked because make local-dev sets the vars to 1 and make local-live-dev sets them to empty (which both work), but anyone setting them by hand will be surprised.

Stakes: AE200_SIMULATOR specifically decides whether commands reach REAL HVAC hardware. A simulator flag that is wrong-way-round is highest-stakes here -- e.g. intending live control but accidentally simulating, or vice versa.

Fix: make AE200_SIMULATOR and AIRTHINGS_SIMULATOR use the same tolerant truthy check as app/hubitat.py (the TRUE_ENV_VALUES = {1,true,yes,on} helper). Consider extracting one shared helper used by all three integrations.
acceptance_criteria: AE200_SIMULATOR and AIRTHINGS_SIMULATOR treat '0'/'false'/'' as OFF, consistent with HUBITAT_SIMULATOR; ideally one shared env-parsing helper

title: AUTO mode setpoints/band are read-only; /set_temp only writes single SetTemp
description:
Context: PR #150 made AUTO (and DRY) settable AE-200 modes -- set_mode() now allows {FAN,COOL,DRY,HEAT,AUTO} and POST /set_mode can put a unit into AUTO. An AE-200 unit exposes five setpoint fields: SetTemp (single active setpoint, used by COOL/HEAT/DRY/FAN), and SetTemp1 (cool), SetTemp2 (heat), AutoMin, AutoMax (the dual-setpoint band used by AUTO mode).

Read/write asymmetry: app/ae200.py extract_set_temperatures() promotes ALL FIVE fields into the app JSON (set_temp_c, cool_set_temp_c, heat_set_temp_c, auto_min_c, auto_max_c), so the system reads/surfaces them. But the WRITE path set_set_temp() only ever sends {"SetTemp": ...}. There is no function that writes SetTemp1, SetTemp2, AutoMin, or AutoMax.

Consequences:
1. An operator can enter AUTO (a settable mode) but cannot adjust the cooling setpoint, heating setpoint, or the band through this system -- those four fields are effectively read-only.
2. Writing SetTemp while a unit is in AUTO has undefined/unverified effect: AUTO control keys off SetTemp1/SetTemp2, so the single SetTemp the code can write may be ignored or treated as a midpoint depending on controller config. The one knob exposed in AUTO is the one whose behavior is unclear here.

Evidence (prod snapshot): a historical AUTO reading on Greenhouse (device 36) showed SetTemp=20.5 while SetTemp1=24 / SetTemp2=19 / AutoMin=20 / AutoMax=25 -- the active band (24/19) was untouchable while the only writable field (20.5) had no clear role.

Severity: latent. AUTO is rare (~13 readings ever, none currently active) and COOL/HEAT/DRY/FAN are correctly served by the single SetTemp. The gap is that AUTO was made reachable without extending the setpoint write path to its dual-setpoint/band model.

Fix direction: either (a) add write support for SetTemp1/SetTemp2 (and AutoMin/AutoMax) so AUTO can be driven, with UI affordances; or (b) if AUTO is not intended for operator setpoint control, document that and restrict/annotate the AUTO selection so it is clear the band is controller-managed, not app-managed.
acceptance_criteria: Either AUTO-mode setpoints (SetTemp1/SetTemp2 and/or AutoMin/AutoMax) are writable through the app, or AUTO's read-only-setpoint behavior is explicitly documented and surfaced in the UI

title: Most HVAC commands logged to changelog with blank comment (set-temp/drive/fan)
description:
Context: the changelog table is the audit trail for manual HVAC changes. After the AE-200 control expansion (modes, set-temp, set-range), only some change types write a descriptive 'comment': 'set range', 'calculated temp multiplier for source N', and rules actions ('rules disabled for ...'). 

Problem: the most common live commands -- set-temp, drive on/off, and fan-speed changes -- are written with a BLANK comment. Verified in a fresh prod snapshot: ~1275 of the changelog rows have an empty comment, and they are exactly the set-temp/drive/fan changes (e.g. unit=1, current_values=22, new_value=21.5; or 1 -> 0 for drive). Only ~256 rows besides 'rules disable' carry a self-describing comment.

Impact: the highest-frequency operator actions are the least self-describing entries in the audit log. Anyone reading changelog has to infer the change type from the (unit, current_values, new_value) shape and the agent string, rather than reading it directly. Mode changes are also sparse/!inconsistently labeled (only 3 mode changes recorded ever).

Fix direction: have set_body_set_temp / set_body_drive / set_body_fan_speed / set_body_mode in app/rules_engine.py write a consistent human-readable comment (e.g. 'set temp 22.0 -> 21.5 C', 'drive ON -> OFF', 'fan HIGH -> MID2', 'mode COOL -> AUTO'), matching the style already used for set range and temp multipliers.
acceptance_criteria: set-temp, drive, fan-speed, and mode changes each write a descriptive changelog comment consistent with the existing 'set range' style

title: Flyway version pinned in CI but not on the prod deploy host (slg1)
description:
Context: a fix commit pinned the Flyway install version in Linux CI. However 'make deploy' runs on host slg1 using whatever 'flyway' binary is installed there; nothing pins or checks that version.

Problem: Flyway checksums are generally version-stable, but version drift between CI and prod is a classic source of surprise 'flyway validate' failures and subtle behavioral differences in migration application. CI green does not guarantee prod-host parity.

Fix direction: pin the Flyway version on the prod host to match CI (or have 'make deploy' assert a minimum/exact Flyway version before migrating), and document the required version in doc/sql-migrations.md.
acceptance_criteria: prod host Flyway version is pinned/asserted to match CI; required version documented

title: device_type backfill (V6) is a one-shot heuristic with no enforcement for new devices
acceptance_criteria: new controllable devices always get a non-null device_type; a check/test flags ae200 devices missing device_type

title: Widen room control buttons to fill full row width
description: On room dashboard control cards (ERV + FCU), the speed buttons are fixed 110px and the row is capped at 600px (desktop), leaving empty space on the sides. Make the buttons equal-width and grow to fill the full available row width, preserving the current non-uniform spacing (1em gaps plus the extra 0.5em margin after the Off button).
notes: Approach: change .speed-btn from fixed width:110px/flex-shrink:0 to flex:1 1 0; min-width:0 (keep height:110px -> wider rectangles, approved). Remove desktop max-width:600px cap and inert justify-content:center. Option A (mobile included): remove now-dead width:90px in @media max-width:768px so mobile buttons also fill-and-fit (fixes prior nowrap overflow). Gaps (1em) + Off margin-right(0.5em) preserved as fixed spacing -> equal widths with non-uniform spacing.
close_reason: Buttons now flex:1 1 0 to equal widths filling full row width; removed 600px desktop cap, dead mobile width, and inert justify-content:center

title: Remove italicized secondary room name from sensor tiles
description: On room dashboard pages, each Temperature Sensors tile shows an italicized secondary line (sensor.room, e.g. 'Lobby' under 'Lobby Sensor'). Remove this secondary name from the tiles.
close_reason: Removed italicized secondary room name (.sensor-room) from sensor tiles plus its dead CSS and the now-redundant single-child wrapper div

title: Add no-return Rooms menu items for Kitchen and Hickory
description: The Rooms dropdown links to /kitchen?embedded and /hickory?embedded; the ?embedded flag renders a '← Main' back button so users can return. Add two additional menu items 'Kitchen (no-return)' and 'Hickory (no-return)' that link to /kitchen and /hickory WITHOUT the ?embedded flag, so the dashboards open with no return navigation.
close_reason: Added Hickory (no-return) and Kitchen (no-return) menu items without the ?embedded flag, grouped alphabetically in app/templates/base.html

title: Duplicate temperature_utils.js include breaks JS on room dashboard
description: room_dashboard.html re-includes /static/temperature_utils.js although base.html (which it extends) already loads it, causing 'Identifier USE_FAHRENHEIT has already been declared' (SyntaxError) on the page. Remove the redundant include in room_dashboard.html.

title: Room dashboard: stale 'was X' label during fast transitions
description: During rapid speed/drive changes, the Off button's historical 'was X' note can show a stale speed because a lagging /status poll overwrites lastDeviceSpeed mid-flurry. Fix: don't update lastDeviceSpeed from polled data while a change is pending for that device (only trust the poll once settled). Active highlighting is already correct; this is the historical label only.
notes: Fixed: updateDeviceStatus now only adopts the polled speed into lastDeviceSpeed in the settled branch (no pending / matched / expired). While a pending optimistic change is held, lastDeviceSpeed is left as the optimistically-set value, so the Off button's 'was X' note reflects the true running speed at click time rather than a lagging poll. Verified via mocked set_*/status: HI then Off under lagging on@LO polls now shows 'Off / was HI'.

title: Extend click-to-chart to /air-quality page
description: The /air-quality page's Indoor table shows the same metrics as the home-page Air Quality section (CO2, Humidity, PM1, PM2.5, Radon, Temp, VOC). Those cells should also be clickable to open the corresponding metric chart, matching the behavior just shipped on / (hvac-9nf). Pressure is excluded (no chart page exists for it).
close_reason: Shipped. /air-quality indoor cells now clickable (CO2, Humidity, PM1, PM2.5, Pressure, Radon, Temp, VOC); added pressure as 7th metric; extracted shared clickable_cells.js and aq_metrics.py.

title: Add CSV download to metric and lighting chart pages
description: Temperature chart has a CSV download button (see app/templates/temperature_chart.html). The new /metric_chart page (hvac-9nf) and the existing /lighting_chart page should also offer CSV download of the currently-displayed series. Follow the temperature chart's pattern.

title: Home page: show time until rules re-enable
description: On the home page, add a new column that, when rules have been disabled for a device, shows the remaining hours:minutes until the rule will automatically re-enable.
notes:
Design decisions (2026-04-20):
- Label: 'Resume'
- Placement: right after Unit column, rowspan=2 in ERV/FCU tables only (Air Quality skipped — no rules applied there)
- Format: H:MM (e.g. '2:15', '0:30'); dash '—' when rules are active
- Effective timer = max(per-device disabled_until, master rules_engine disabled_until). Option A.
- Impl: add 'rules_master_disabled_until' as top-level key in /api/v1/status response (since rules_engine pseudo-device has no devlog row and is excluded from get_device_status). Compute effective client-side.
- Refresh reuses existing 1-sec refreshGridRows tick.
- Existing 'rules disabled' superscript kept for now (user: 'mostly for debugging, will remove soon').
2026-04-20 (round 2):
- Column renamed 'Resume Rules' → 'Disable for' (matches common UX phrasing better than 'Disabled Until' since the displayed value is remaining duration).
- Added −/+ adjustment buttons in each row's cell, styled like settemp thermostat widget.
- Semantics: +/- modify per-device disabled_until (not the global timer); hidden when rules active (dash). + snaps up to next 30-min boundary, − snaps down; if result <= now it clamps to 0 (re-enables).
- New endpoint: POST /api/v1/set_device_disabled_until body {device_id, disabled_until}; past timestamp clamps to 0.
- Dropped all_rules_disabled_until from /status since per-device is now authoritative for this column.
2026-04-20 (round 2 — correction):
Rounding is applied to *remaining minutes* (duration), not wall-clock time. The click reads the currently displayed minute count (ceil seconds/60), and snaps UP for + or DOWN for − to the nearest multiple of 30. This is drift-free: e.g. clicking + when '1:00' is displayed always yields 90 min, regardless of sub-minute jitter from the 1-sec refresh.
2026-04-20 (final):
- Optimistic UI: button clicks update the cell immediately and debounce the server POST by 400ms so rapid clicks coalesce. Refresh loop skips server updates for a device while its write is pending; a sequence number disambiguates late-resolving older POSTs.
- Cell centering: column text-align changed to center so rows with/without buttons line up vertically.
- Renamed HTML IDs and CSS classes from 'resume' to 'disable-for' for consistency with the final column label.

title: Migrate beads from server mode to embedded mode
description: This project was initialized when beads v0.55-0.56 only supported server mode. As of v0.63.3/v1.0.0, embedded mode is the default and simpler (no dolt-server process to manage). Migration path: bd backup init, bd backup sync, bd init (re-initialize as embedded), bd backup restore --force.

title: Use per-device API calls in hickory_room_status
description:
hickory_room_status (routes_api.py) currently calls hubitat.get_all_devices() and filters by ID to read attributes like level and switch. Some Hubitat Maker API firmware versions don't return full attributes on the all-devices endpoint, which would cause the dimmer to always show 0% and lights to show off.

Switch to calling hubitat.get_device_info(device_id) for each configured device (dimmer_id, wall_inner_id, wall_outer_id). This trades 1 HTTP call for 3, but guarantees full attribute data.

This also resolves the dead-code issue: get_device_info() in hubitat.py was added in the hickory-room branch but has no callers yet.
notes:
Implementation plan:
1. In hickory_room_status(), replace the get_all_devices() + by_id lookup with individual get_device_info() calls for each configured device ID
2. Wrap each call in its own try/except so one device being unreachable doesn't break the whole response
3. Update test_room_status_returns_device_states to mock hubitat.get_device_info instead of get_all_devices
4. Update test_room_status_missing_devices — get_device_info will raise or return empty for missing devices
5. Verify against the actual Hubitat hub that attributes (level, switch) are present in the single-device response

title: Humidity coloring has no 'fair' band on the dry side (hard good->poor cliff at 30%)
description:
Context: in app/static/air_quality_coloring.js + air_quality_thresholds.json, humidity grades good -> fair (>50) -> poor (>60) on the high side, but on the low side it jumps straight from good to poor at poorBelow=30 with no intermediate band: 31% = air-good, 29% = air-poor.

Problem: asymmetric UX -- the dry side has no 'fair' warning buffer that the humid side has. A user sees no gradual cue as humidity drops toward the poor threshold. Note the classifier currently supports only poorBelow (no fairBelow), so adding a dry-side fair band is a small feature, not just a threshold tweak.

Fix direction: add a 'fairBelow' rule (e.g. fairBelow 40) handled in airQualityClassForValue(), so e.g. <30 poor, 30-40 fair, 40-50 good, >50 fair, >60 poor; add a test case mirroring the existing humidity boundary tests.
acceptance_criteria: Humidity (and any two-sided metric) supports a fairBelow band; dry-side grading is good/fair/poor symmetric with the humid side; boundary test added

title: Hubitat simulator fixture is served in local-dev but exercised by no test
description:
Context: there are two separate Hubitat JSON fixtures with different shapes:
- app/test_data/hubitat_get_devices.json -- 17 devices, 'attributes' as a DICT (e.g. {"temperature":"19.4","humidity":"15",...}). This is what the HUBITAT_SIMULATOR serves from get_all_devices().
- etc/sample_hubitat.json -- a DIFFERENT file/shape, which tests/test_hubitat.py loads to validate extract_temperatures() and update_from_hubitat().

Problem: the simulator fixture (hubitat_get_devices.json) is referenced by ZERO tests. So the exact JSON that 'make local-dev' feeds through extract_temperatures()/update_from_hubitat() is never validated by the suite. If its shape drifts from what the parser expects, tests stay green while local-dev silently produces wrong or empty sensor data -- defeating the simulator's purpose. The two fixtures already have visibly different 'attributes' structures, so their interchangeability is unverified.

Fix direction: cover the simulator fixture with a test (e.g. run app/test_data/hubitat_get_devices.json through extract_temperatures()/update_from_hubitat() and assert sane temps), or consolidate to a single shared Hubitat fixture used by both the simulator and the tests.
acceptance_criteria: The JSON served by HUBITAT_SIMULATOR is exercised by at least one test (or a single shared fixture is used by both simulator and tests)

title: Hubitat simulator is read-only; command/write paths still hit real hardware
description:
Context: HUBITAT_SIMULATOR mode (PR for 'full implementation of hubitat simulator') stubs only the READ path. app/hubitat.py get_all_devices() returns app/test_data/hubitat_get_devices.json when the simulator is enabled, but the command/write helpers are NOT simulator-aware:
- send_device_command() always builds a real URL and does requests.get(...)
- get_device_info() always does real HTTP
- set_dimmer_level() / set_switch() go through send_device_command()

Effect: under 'make local-dev' (which sets HUBITAT_SIMULATOR=1), reading sensor temperatures works offline, but any Hubitat COMMAND fires a real HTTP request to the configured hubitat.host. In a dev environment that host is unreachable -> a TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2 timeout/error. Concrete exposure: the Hickory room dashboard (app/room_config.py) has tv_control=True, a dimmer_id, and inner/outer wall switches; exercising those controls in local-dev hits the real-network path, not the simulator.

Contrast: the AE-200 simulator is complete -- set_drive/set_fan_speed/set_mode/set_set_temp all check AE200_SIMULATOR and mutate simulated_devices. The Hubitat simulator only got the read half, and this asymmetry is undocumented.

Action: (1) document the read-only scope (in the Makefile simulator notes and/or doc) so developers know commands are not simulated; (2) consider making send_device_command()/get_device_info() simulator-aware (no-op or fixture-backed state) so room-dashboard controls are testable offline.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only scope of the Hubitat simulator is documented; optionally, Hubitat command/write paths are simulator-aware so local-dev never makes real Hubitat HTTP calls

title: Generalize hardcoded /hickory/ API routes for any room
description:
The four Hickory room control endpoints (room_status, dimmer, wall_light, tv) are hardcoded under /api/v1/hickory/ and look up room_config.ROOM_CONFIGS.get('hickory', {}). If another room (e.g. kitchen) ever needs similar controls, these routes would need to be duplicated.

Refactor to accept the room name as a URL parameter (e.g. /api/v1/room/<location>/dimmer) and look up the config dynamically, similar to how routes_web.py already handles /kitchen and /hickory with a shared _render_room_dashboard_with_data().
notes: Only worth doing when a second room actually needs controls. Not a bug — just coupling to watch for.
